REL-328.name: Pointer Taken From a Temporary That Is Dropped at Once
REL-328.question: Does this function take a raw pointer from a temporary owner that is dropped at the end of the same statement, and use the pointer afterwards?

rust: CString::new(s).unwrap().as_ptr() stored in a variable or passed on after the statement ends
as_ptr() or as_mut_ptr() called on a temporary String, Vec, Box or to_owned() result, such as s.to_string().as_ptr()
a pointer from as_ptr() used after the owning Vec or String was pushed to, reallocated, moved or dropped
the owner is bound to a variable that outlives every use of the pointer
the temporary's pointer is used only inside the same full expression, such as as an argument of one call
ownership is handed over with into_raw and later reclaimed with from_raw

distinguish_from.CWE-416: the memory was freed explicitly rather than by a temporary's drop at the end of a statement

REL-329.name: Aliasing or Mutability Rules Broken Through Raw Pointers
REL-329.question: Does unsafe code in this function create references that break Rust's aliasing rules, such as a mutable reference alongside another reference to the same data?

rust: a shared reference or *const T cast to *mut T and written through, or turned into &mut T, where the data is not inside an UnsafeCell
two &mut references to the same or overlapping memory made from one raw pointer, or &mut *ptr while another reference to the target is live
transmute from &T to &mut T, or a function returning &mut T derived from a &self or &T argument
static mut read or written through references from code that may run on several threads or re-entrantly
interior mutability goes through UnsafeCell, Cell, RefCell, a lock or an atomic
disjoint parts are split with split_at_mut or by borrowing separate fields
the raw pointer is the only access path while the mutable reference lives

distinguish_from.REL-007: the cast is flagged only for hiding its target type behind an underscore
distinguish_from.CWE-362: the access is a data race between threads rather than an aliasing rule broken within one

REL-330.name: Panic That Can Unwind Out of an extern "C" Function or Callback
REL-330.question: Is this function called from foreign code, and can it panic so that unwinding would cross the foreign boundary?

rust: an extern "C" fn or #[no_mangle] function whose body calls unwrap, expect, panic!, assert!, indexes a slice, or divides by a value that may be zero
a Rust closure or function passed as a callback to a C library that can panic
arguments from foreign code, such as pointers and lengths, used in operations that panic on bad values
the body is wrapped in std::panic::catch_unwind and a failure is turned into an error code
every fallible step returns an error value instead of panicking
the function uses the "C-unwind" ABI on purpose, or the crate aborts on panic and that is the intended behaviour

distinguish_from.CWE-754: the missing check matters whether or not the caller is foreign code
